data.note: Toy phase and baseline runner under demos/, sandbox only, stub worker; ddflow metrics swarm view plus the provider.

data.summary: In the gap between ddflow merge (lease released) and ddflow complete, ddflow next offers the merged item as ready and a claim by ANY other agent succeeds as a rework: item.reworked clears every gate, so the merging lane's complete is refused (implement, unit_tests, merge 'not run') and the second lane holds an empty item. Hit by 3 stub lanes in a sandbox in the first full run of SW-pilot-toy (toy-08: lane-1 merge 13:57:23, lane-2 claim 13:57:24 and item.reworked with the merged sha), and reproduced by hand with two agents: merge as lane-1, next as lane-2 lists it, claim as lane-2 exits 0, complete as lane-1 exits 3. Every parallel fleet has this race; any pull lane (SW-pull) makes it routine. The re-claim route of fix-B-rework-of-merged-item-keeps-stale-merge is for a deliberate rework. Direction: next does not offer an item with a merge and no completion, and a claim of one by an agent other than the merger is refused unless it says it means rework. Regression test: two agents, merge then next and claim, gates intact and complete passes. SW-pilot-toy works around it by never letting a lane claim an item another lane took in the run; real lanes share no such board.
data.title: A merged item not yet completed is offered and claimable: a second lane's claim wipes its gates

data.body:
Fixes bug B-merged-uncompleted-claimable: In the gap between ddflow merge (lease released) and ddflow complete, ddflow next offers the merged item as ready and a claim by ANY other agent succeeds as a rework: item.reworked clears every gate, so the merging lane's complete is refused (implement, unit_tests, merge 'not run') and the second lane holds an empty item. Hit by 3 stub lanes in a sandbox in the first full run of SW-pilot-toy (toy-08: lane-1 merge 13:57:23, lane-2 claim 13:57:24 and item.reworked with the merged sha), and reproduced by hand with two agents: merge as lane-1, next as lane-2 lists it, claim as lane-2 exits 0, complete as lane-1 exits 3. Every parallel fleet has this race; any pull lane (SW-pull) makes it routine. The re-claim route of fix-B-rework-of-merged-item-keeps-stale-merge is for a deliberate rework. Direction: next does not offer an item with a merge and no completion, and a claim of one by an agent other than the merger is refused unless it says it means rework. Regression test: two agents, merge then next and claim, gates intact and complete passes. SW-pilot-toy works around it by never letting a lane claim an item another lane took in the run; real lanes share no such board. Found on SW-pilot-toy.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-merged-uncompleted-claimable --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-merged-uncompleted-claimable --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B-merged-uncompleted-claimable: A merged item not yet completed is offered and claimable: a second lane's cla...

data.budget: 15 min, no live model, no GPU
data.claim: With stub workers, three lanes on the 12-item toy phase merge more than 1.8x the items per hour of one lane, all 12 on their gates with no override, and nothing reaches the host repository.
data.falsifier: A ratio near 1 at three lanes, an override or forced completion in the sandbox log, or a sandbox head known to the host.
data.mechanism: Each item's verbs run in its own worktree and only merge serialises on the sandbox main, so verb overhead (about 8 s per item) parallelises across lanes; a chain of 4 over 12 items leaves a ceiling of 3x.
data.probe: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py setup/run/report, one pair at --work-s 2 and one at --work-s 0, on this host at load average 75 to 117
data.probe_output: work-s 2: 387.88 -> 973.01 merged items per hour (2.51x), rework 8.33% both, agent-hours per item 0.0018 -> 0.0017. work-s 0: 459.52 -> 1248.92 (2.72x), rework 8.33% both, 0.0014 -> 0.0013. 12 of 12 merged, overrides 0, isolated true on all four sides. Stub time only: this measures ddflow overhead, not a pilot. First 3-lane attempt failed on B-merged-uncompleted-claimable (toy-08), filed; lanes now share a board.
data.question: Can a sandbox toy phase and one runner measure one lane against three through the real CLI, and is ddflow's own coordination a bottleneck at three lanes?

evidence.note: R20ea31dfa7 CONFIRMED: two stub pairs through the real CLI, 2.51x and 2.72x, 12 of 12 merged, overrides 0, isolated true; falsifier stated in the note.

Read D-swarm-pilot-2026-11-05, D-swarm-answers Q4, r-adapters, r-consent-outward, r-safe-by-default, r-bounded-everything, r-docs-with-the-change, r-surface-budget, r-no-eager-heavy-import, r-task-phase-needs-wave. The sandbox has a deadline and call timeouts; metrics help and goldens regenerated in the change; no new knob; the agent-hours ratio no longer judges the dollar target, per D-swarm-pilot point 3.

d6fe74d8b: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py and swarm_pilot_run.py, ddflow metrics swarm view, provider wired through the shared Registry, compare leaves targets.cost None on agent-hours, research note. pytest tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py tests/test_swarm_metrics.py passes.

chunk_findings.detail: `agent_s = _held_s(ctx.facts, items, ctx.now) + _review_s(ctx.facts, items)` returns `0.0` when a repository has no `held` or `review` facts but has merged items (e.g., a sandbox/toy runner that records only completed states and no agent-hold records). The new metric `swarm.agent_hours_per_item` then emits `0.0` instead of `None`, and the new `text()` output prints `0.0000` under "agent-hours per item". That misrepresents absent measurement as a real zero agent-time figure; only `None` is rendered as `UNAVAILABLE`, so the view claims zero work was done rather than "unavailable", skewing the cost figure the change is supposed to model.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm_metrics.py provider

chunk_findings.detail: `judge` always returns `"compare": S.compare(before, after)` even when `comparable` is false. Concrete input: two sandboxes run with `--work-s 2` and `--work-s 4` produce a `why_not` entry for `work_s differs`, so the report says `"comparable": false`, but `report --json` still contains `compare.targets.throughput`, `compare.targets.rework`, and `compare.targets.cost` verdicts. A JSON consumer can read a target verdict for a pair the function says is not judged, contradicting the function's own contract and `render`'s human view.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:judge

chunk_findings.detail: There is no `lanes >= 1` validation. `python demos/swarm_pilot_run.py run DIR --lanes 0` (or a negative count) writes `lanes: 0` into the manifest, creates zero threads, sees no board failure, prints `ran 0 lane(s)`, and exits 0. This falsely records a sandbox as successfully run with no work done; the CLI should refuse non-positive lane counts.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: Unlike `guard_new`, `Sandbox.open` never rejects a path that is an ancestor of `ROOT`. Input: host repository is `[REDACTED:path]`; create `[REDACTED:path]` as its own git work tree with no remote and place `[REDACTED:path]` there. `Sandbox.open(Path("[REDACTED:path]"))` resolves the path, sees it is not inside the host, sees the manifest exists, passes `check()`, and returns a `Sandbox`. A subsequent `sb.ddflow("task", "add", ...)` runs `ddflow --repo [REDACTED:path]`, whose work tree contains the host repository, so the sandbox is not isolated from the host.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.open

chunk_findings.detail: The task-add loop adds every item with `--phase` and either `--needs <deps>` or `--tags no-deps`, but it never supplies a `wave:N` tag and never runs `ddflow waves --stamp`. This violates [r-task-phase-needs-wave], which requires every task to carry a `wave:N` tag; `no-deps` is not that wave tag. Running `setup()` on a fresh path creates 12 tasks without the required wave tag.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:setup

chunk_findings.detail: The documented agent-hours formula is “lease-held time plus recorded review time.” But the same document’s lane sequence is `claim`, `gate record` and `gate run`, `merge`, `complete`: a review recorded by `gate run` happens before `merge`, while the item is still lease-held. That review time is therefore already inside lease-held time, so adding it again double-counts it. Any real-lane run with a review gate (the setup this document explicitly tells SW-pilot-local to enable) inflates `swarm.agent_hours_per_item` and the `swarm_metrics.compare` `cost_x` ratio. The figure should not sum the two intervals; it should use a non-overlapping calculation such as lease-held time only, or subtract review time from lease-held time before adding it.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/swarm-pilot-toy.md:50

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `"cost_usd" in ans.text` only proves the label appears. A regressed view that still prints a skewed dollar figure (for example `cost_usd: 1.3`) when the log records no dollars would satisfy this test even though the comment claims it verifies “no dollars are recorded, and the view says so.” The test never asserts the value is `n/a` or absent, so the exact skewed-figure regression this change is meant to prevent is not caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_metrics.py:test_the_swarm_view_prints_the_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: `_git` runs `git -C <repo> ...` with whatever environment the pytest process inherited, without removing `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`. In an environment where these variables point at the host repository (the exact `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` attack the sandbox guard is supposed to neutralize), `git -C` does not override them. Concretely, in `test_a_linked_worktree_with_a_manifest_is_refused`, `_git(main, "worktree", "add", "-q", str(linked))` would add `<tmp>/linked` as a worktree of the **host** repository, mutating the host `.git/worktrees` metadata. This makes the new test suite itself touch the host under that environment, directly refuting the “sandbox never touches the host” guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py:_git

chunk_findings.detail: `_isolated` treats every non-zero `git cat-file -e` as "HEAD is unknown to the host". It also runs that probe with `env=sb.env`, so a sandbox env that makes host git fail (empty `PATH`, bad `GIT_EXEC_PATH`, `safe.directory` rejection, `GIT_DIR` pointing at a missing path) yields returncode 128/127, not 1. Given a sandbox whose `main` is a host commit and `git remote` is empty, `_isolated` returns True, `judge` sets `comparable`, and `render` can print throughput/rework `met` for a tree that is not isolated from the host.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:201

chunk_findings.detail: `run` builds lanes with `range(1, lanes + 1)` and treats an empty thread list as success. `python3 demos/swarm_pilot_run.py run DIR --lanes 0` (or `--lanes -1`) writes the manifest, starts no workers, never calls `Board.over`, leaves every item undone, and exits 0 with `ran 0 lane(s)`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:186

chunk_findings.detail: `Board.over` reads and sorts `self.left` outside `self.lock`, then calls `fail` before re-checking under the lock. If the deadline fires as the last lane `finish`es the last item, `over` still records `deadline: N item(s) left` and `run` raises `RunFailed` after a complete phase. Concurrent `discard` during `sorted(self.left)` can also raise `RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration` and fail the run the same way.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:122

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.__init__` stores any path and `git`/`ddflow` never call `check` or `guard_new`. `Sandbox(ROOT).must("merge", "toy-01")` runs `python -m ddflow --repo <host>` with the host checkout as `--repo`, so the sandbox harness mutates the host repository. The comments claim construction only through `setup`/`open`; that is not enforced on the methods that actually spawn processes.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:156

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.open` refuses a path inside the host but not a path that contains the host (`host.is_relative_to(real)` is only in `guard_new`). Given host `/work/proj` and an outer git repo `/work` with no remotes and `.ddflow/local/swarm-pilot.json` present, `Sandbox.open(Path("/work"))` succeeds, then `git`/`ddflow --repo /work` operate on a work tree that holds the host checkout.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:162

chunk_findings.detail: `clean_env` copies `TMPDIR` and `PATH` from the parent process. With `TMPDIR` set to a directory inside the host (for example `$HOST/tmp`) and `setup(Path("/tmp/pilot-sb"))` otherwise passing `guard_new`, `git` and the ddflow child still use that `TMPDIR` and can create files in the host. A `PATH` entry inside the host is also executed when resolving `git`/`python`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: `--lanes` is an unconstrained int. `run(sb, 0, worker)` (CLI: `run DIR --lanes 0`, also any `lanes < 1`) builds an empty thread list, never calls `Board.over`, leaves `board.failure` empty, and returns success after writing `lanes` into the manifest. The sandbox is then marked already-run, so a later real run is refused, while no item was claimed or merged.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: `over` reads and `sorted(self.left)` outside `self.lock` while `finish` discards from that set. With the deadline already passed and at least one item still in `left`, one lane in `over` and another in `finish` makes `sorted` raise `RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration`. That exception is caught in `_lane` and stored as the run failure, so a run that actually finished every item is reported as `RunFailed`. The same unlocked check can call `fail` after the last `finish`, which also sets `failure` on a completed board.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:Board.over

chunk_findings.detail: `_why_not` never requires the two sides to differ in `lanes`, and `judge` always attaches `S.compare` (including target booleans) even when `why_not` is non-empty. `report A B --json` therefore emits `compare.targets` as met/NOT MET for two equal-lane sandboxes, or for a pair with overrides / a non-isolated sandbox, while the text path prints `NOT COMPARABLE`. Swapping a 1-lane and a 3-lane directory judges the throughput target in the wrong direction with no refusal.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:judge

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.git` forwards every argument after `git -C <sandbox>`, and `check` only runs at open/setup, not on each call. `sb.git("--git-dir", "<host>/.git", "commit", ...)` (or `sb.git("config", "core.worktree", "<host>")` followed by a write) operates on the host repository even though path guards passed and the sandbox has no remote.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: `guard_new` refuses a directory that contains the host (`host.is_relative_to(real)`), but `open` does not. Given a parent of the host that is its own work tree, has `.ddflow/local/swarm-pilot.json`, and has no remotes, `open` succeeds; a later `git add` or task whose glob reaches the nested host tree writes the host checkout.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.open

chunk_findings.detail: The allow-list copies `TMPDIR` unchanged. With `TMPDIR` set to a directory inside the host repository, every sandbox `git`/`ddflow` process inherits that path and can create temp files in the host tree, which the “never touches the host” guard never checks.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:clean_env
